Consider the region $D$ shown above. If 

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}{e}^{x+y}, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,{∬}_{D}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

Require $D\subseteq R$, so the rectangle contains the entire region. Which of the following could be the definition of the rectangular domain $R?$

- $R=[-1,3]\times [-2,1]$
- $R=[-1,2]\times [-2,2]$
- $R=[-2,3]\times [-2,2]$

authoring.value:
The displayed region includes points with $y>1$, so rectangle I, $[-1,3]\times[-2,1]$, does not contain all of $D$. It includes points with $x>2$, so rectangle II, $[-1,2]\times[-2,2]$, also fails the containment requirement. The entire drawn region lies in rectangle III, $[-2,3]\times[-2,2]$.

For rectangle III, $f=e^{x+y}$ on $D$ and zero on $R\setminus D$, giving $\iint_R f\,dA=\iint_De^{x+y}\,dA$. Therefore the answer is "III only".
